key_insight: Under strong adverse pressure gradients, turbulent boundary layers retain component-wise outer similarity when each velocity defect or Reynolds stress is normalized by its own value at a shared outer-layer location.
engineering_relevance: Compact outer-profile expressions offer references for assessing APG turbulence models and reconstructing profiles when component amplitudes are known.
method: Combine separation-bubble DNS with published turbulent-boundary-layer profiles.
Normalize two mean-velocity defects and four Reynolds stresses by their respective values at a common location, illustrated at y_s = 0.5δ.
Assess profile collapse across conditions and test sensitivity to the normalization location.
evidence_signal: Across β_e = 0.04–180 and Re_θ = 530–19,000, collapse emerges at y/δ ≳ 0.2 for velocity defects and ≳ 0.4 for Reynolds stresses, and persists over a broad range of outer normalization locations.
watch_item: The similarity is component-wise and outer-layer-specific; reconstruction still requires each quantity’s value at the chosen normalization location.
paper_title: Component-wise outer similarity of turbulent boundary layers with strong adverse-pressure gradient
